_spec: Companion job for the GE16 weekly chain: the OPS chain orchestrator. The record is DECLARED in the canonical registry OPS/cron/ge16_jobs.json as the optional seventh job (id ge16-chain, enabled=false, state=disabled, non_blocking=false), pinned by sync_jobs.validate_canonical_config + the OPS contract's scheduler_binding, and its contract is pinned by validate_ops_contract._validate_optional_chain_cron_contract. The job is the owner-visible START of the chain, not the work itself: the owner-side listener OPS/cron/ge16_chain_runner.py (launchd label com.tenunan.ge16-chain) owns minting and stage execution. Enabling it is an owner decision: the record ships disabled and only an owner-authorized live cron change may flip that.

job.name: GE16 P1.6 OPS Chain Orchestrator (optional)
job.gate_note: The chain job writes chain evidence only (OPS/logs/chain) and owns no domain gate. It starts the run and stages 2-5 advance only when the predecessor handoff manifest validates by content hash; a stop is recorded, never retried out of order, and the five stage jobs stay scheduled as the fallback floor.

agent_scope.executes: Stage 1 only (phase a, judgement, phase b), with owner-minted keys the daemon placed in the one-shot directory
agent_scope.does_not_execute: Stages 2-5; those are launched by the owner-side chain listener or by their own stage job
never: mint or hand-write a fire key
write a pipeline domain outside its own Stage 1 execution

chain_mode.on_demand_trigger: python3 OPS/cron/ge16_chain_runner.py --start (starts or resumes this chain week's run and surfaces Stage 1's phase a and phase b keys)
chain_mode.anchor: Friday 22:00 Asia/Kuala_Lumpur, the chain job's own schedule
chain_mode.stage_five_window_note: Stage 5 is owner-authorized release work that runs on its own 05:30 schedule after the Stage 4 handoff, so the listener bounds its wait by the 12-hour run deadline instead of a 45-minute window a healthy week could never meet; the 45-minute figure is the Stage 5 job's own inactivity limit.
chain_mode.completion_rule: a stage counts as complete only when its handoff manifest is present, differs by content hash from the snapshot taken at run start, and (stage 2 onwards) cites the recorded SHA-256 of the immediate predecessor manifest
chain_mode.failure_rule: any failed stage stops the chain without advancing; the run stays recorded and the next weekly run resumes at the first un-completed stage
chain_mode.dependency: chain mode mints and fires through the existing scheduled-fire path, so the four stage job records must stay enabled/scheduled in the live registry and the existing remint daemon stays installed; its Stage 1 keys are the owner daemon's, never the agent's
chain_mode.optional_authoring_step: not driven by the listener: it is agent-side, non-blocking and ships disabled; the chain proceeds Stage 2 -> Stage 3 regardless
